title: Springer Journal Retracts AI Review After Undeclared Generative AI Use
key_facts: Discover Artificial Intelligence, a Springer Nature journal, retracted a 2024 critical review on AI in communication research; the retraction note was published on 3 Oct 2026 (DOI 10.1007/s44163-026-02440-4).
The paper, by Muhammad Asif and Zhou Gouqing of Hunan Normal University, Changsha, was first published 16 May 2024.
The publisher found a number of citations contextually incorrect, a pattern it said may suggest generative AI was used in writing the manuscript without declaration.
Springer Nature said the authors gave no satisfactory explanation and it no longer has confidence in the article's contents.
Asif disagrees with the retraction; Gouqing did not respond to the publisher.
Major publishers allow limited AI assistance but require disclosure and hold authors responsible for all content including references; the two-year gap illustrates how slow such investigations are.
quote_evidence: Discover Artificial Intelligence, a Springer Nature journal, has formally retracted a 2024 review article ... after the publisher concluded that generative AI had been used in the manuscript without being declared
A number of citations in the paper appeared to be contextually incorrect, a pattern the publisher stated may suggest that generative AI was used in writing the manuscript.
Muhammad Asif disagrees with the retraction, formally registering his objection in the published notice.
why_it_matters_hint: A paper about AI in research was pulled for suspected undeclared AI writing, flagged by its mismatched citations; the publisher acted two years after publication.
notes: Bioengineer.org carries a Scienmag text (bylined Denise Maddox, Scienmag), so Scienmag is the source. The retraction itself is an official publisher record with a DOI.
